gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-gantari: Comic Relief has a bold, hand-cut look, with bowls left unfinished on one side and no shift between its up and side strokes. And Gantari follows with a wire-bent feel and wide apertures, friendly and contemporary where the heading is loud.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-gayathri: Gayathri carries an open-ended look on every curved letter, plus the faint thick-thin variation of a letterpress slug, against a heading of unshaded strokes. Across a full page, that quiet cadence keeps the text moving.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-google-sans: Loud meets tidy here. Comic Relief commands attention with its unfinished bowls and uniform lines, while Google Sans stays friendly and modern, with terminals pulled well back and no thick-thin shift.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-google-sans-flex: Comic Relief is the bold one, its strokes uniform in every direction and its bowls left unfinished on one side. But Google Sans Flex handles the working text, with stroke ends cut like one ribbon and each curve closing on a clean, open gap.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-gothic-a1: Comic Relief hits hard, with flat, single-weight linework and unfinished bowls. Gothic A1 follows in a lower-contrast voice, friendly and businesslike, and its splayed c terminal gives a long stretch of text a gentle, steady rhythm.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-gotu: Strokes of constant width, like bent pipe, give Comic Relief its commanding, unfinished-bowl look. Gotu then takes over the text with clean sans-serif lines, modest hairline thinning at the curves and e crossbars with open mouths.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-gowun-dodum: Bowls left unfinished on one side give Comic Relief a bold, commanding face with no stroke variation. But it earns its keep big and short, while Gowun Dodum offers a smooth, tube-like sans-serif with a wide-mouthed lowercase a.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-gruppo: Commanding is how Comic Relief comes across, its strokes never swelling or thinning and its bowls left unfinished. Gruppo moves through a longer stretch of text more lightly, a clean plain sans whose curve endings never get near each other.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-gudea: Big, blunt and unfinished, Comic Relief draws its bowls open on one side with no difference between up and side strokes. Gudea settles into longer text with sans-serif curves as thin as a drawn thread.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-hanken-grotesk: Bold is the first word for Comic Relief, with its unfinished bowls and strokes that never change direction in weight. But shrink it small and that commanding presence thins out, while Hanken Grotesk keeps its wire-bent, clean lines and wide channels into each counter.
